info.title: Attome XRM API
info.description: The Attome XRM platform's HTTP API. Entity record shapes under `/api/v1/{entity}` are resolved from each deployment's runtime metadata (D-003) and therefore cannot be enumerated statically — those operations document the generic envelope only. Fetch `GET /api/v1/schema/{logicalname}` for a live entity's fields.

delete.description: P8-T1: tokens already issued for it stop working at once.

post.summary: Issue a viewer token for an embed
post.description:
P8-T1: called by the host site's server, never its browser. The token
fixes the given dashboard parameters for one viewer and lives at most an
hour.

422.description: The fixed parameters do not fit in a token

x-audit-exempt.note: signs a short-lived viewer token; nothing is stored

post.description: P8-T1: lets the given sites frame the dashboard, reading as the caller.

422.description: No origins, too many, or one that is not an https origin

post.summary: Create a dashboard from a layout
post.description:
Creates a dashboard and its whole tree of pages, sections and widgets from one layout document in
one transaction, for a caller that has the layout decided already (an AI authoring flow, an
import). Editing an existing dashboard stays the record API's job. Needs the dashboard create
privilege. Audited.

get.description:
Every registered widget type with its descriptor, so a builder can fill its palette without a
hard-coded list. Any signed-in user: it is a list of capabilities, not data.

parameters.name: include_unsupported
parameters.description:
D-525 — include types the viewer cannot render (hidden by default so a
palette only offers renderable widgets).

post.description:
Copies a widget, with its configuration, into its own section or into `target_section_id`. Needs
update rights on widgets and the right to create one. Audited.

Validates a declarative widget's configuration before it is saved through the record API, and
names every problem, so a bad configuration is refused when written rather than when drawn. Writes
nothing. Needs update rights on widgets.

x-audit-exempt.note: pure pre-save config validation; persists nothing

post.description:
A reviewer's sign-off: moves the working copy from review to approved, ready to publish.
Dashboard editors only. Audited.

409.description: Not in review, or row_version is stale

post.description:
Marks the dashboard archived and inactive and clears its published version; the record API's
restore brings it back, still archived. Dashboard editors only. Audited.

409.description: Already archived, or row_version is stale

post.description:
A new draft dashboard named "<name> (Copy)", copied from this one. Dashboard editors only.
Audited.

get.description:
Whether every query and view its widgets name still exists and resolves, so a renamed or deleted
one is found before publishing instead of when a widget fails to draw. Anyone who may read the
dashboard.

post.summary: Add a page to a dashboard
post.description:
Creates the page together with its root grid section in one transaction, under the dashboard's
lifecycle lock. Dashboard editors only. Audited.

201.description: Page created with its root section

409.description: Another request is changing this dashboard

post.description:
Runs every widget of one page over the records the caller may see, in one call. Writes nothing.
Anyone who may read the dashboard.

200.description: Every widget on the page, executed with at most four at a time; a widget that fails carries its own error

404.description: No such dashboard or page in the executed definition

422.description: An unknown parameter or a malformed value

x-audit-exempt.note: Dashboard 10/10 Phase 2.3: executes every widget of one page over the caller's record scope and writes nothing.

post.summary: Give a page its root section
post.description: Adds the root grid section to a page that has none. Needs the right to create sections. Audited.

404.description: No such dashboard, or the page is not on it

409.description: The page already has a section, or the dashboard is busy

post.description:
Writes an approved dashboard's tree as a new immutable version and points viewers at it, pinning
each widget's query to the version it was published with. When `approval.required_actions` gates
it, this submits an approval request instead (202, `approval_pending`) and a second administrator
decides. Dashboard editors only. Audited.

409.description: Not approved, or row_version is stale

get.description:
The snapshot viewers see, which editing the working copy does not change. Anyone who may read
the dashboard.

200.description: What viewers of this dashboard see

post.summary: Send a dashboard back to draft
post.description: Moves the working copy from review back to draft. Dashboard editors only. Audited.

409.description: Not in review, or row_version is stale

post.description:
What `@current_user`, `@current_date` and the dashboard's other variables come to for this
viewer, embed context and URL overrides. Writes nothing. Anyone who may read the dashboard.

x-audit-exempt.note: resolves declared variable/parameter defaults and embed/URL overrides for display; persists nothing

post.description:
Returns the published working copy to draft for editing; viewers keep seeing the published
version. Dashboard editors only. Audited.

200.description: Working copy returned to draft; the live version is unchanged

409.description: Not published, or row_version is stale

post.description: Moves the working copy from draft to review. Dashboard editors only. Audited.

409.description: Not in draft, or row_version is stale

get.description:
The working copy's pages, sections and widgets in one response, for the editor. Needs update
rights on the dashboard.

404.description: No such dashboard, or the caller may not edit it

422.description: The tree exceeds the page, section or widget ceiling

post.description:
Viewers see no published version any more and the working copy returns to draft. Dashboard editors
only. Audited.

409.description: Not published, or row_version is stale

post.summary: Roll a dashboard back to a version
post.description:
Points viewers at an earlier published version, behind the same four-eyes gate as publishing.
Dashboard editors only. Audited.

404.description: No such dashboard, or the version does not belong to it

409.description: row_version is stale, or the dashboard is busy

post.summary: Restore a version into the draft
post.description:
Writes an earlier version's tree into the working copy; what viewers see does not change until it
is published. Dashboard editors only. Audited.

404.description: No such dashboard, or the version does not belong to it

409.description: Another request is already changing this dashboard

post.description:
Runs one widget's definition over the records the caller may see and returns its values. Writes
nothing. Anyone who may read the dashboard.

200.description: The widget's data, executed server-side from the published definition (or the draft for a preview)

404.description: No such dashboard, nothing is published, the widget is not in the executed definition, or a preview without record Update

422.description: An unknown parameter, a malformed value, or a widget whose definition cannot execute

x-audit-exempt.note: Dashboard 10/10 Phase 2.3: executes a widget definition over the caller's record scope and writes nothing.

post.description:
How the widget's value is calculated, from the same resolved context as its data. Writes nothing.
Anyone who may read the dashboard.

200.description: How the widget's number is calculated, from the same context the data route uses

404.description: No such dashboard, nothing is published, or the widget is not in the executed definition

422.description: An unknown parameter, a malformed value, or a definition that cannot execute

x-audit-exempt.note: Dashboard 10/10 Phase 3.2: explains how a widget value is calculated from the same resolved context and writes nothing.

post.summary: List the records behind a widget value
post.description:
The records the caller may see that make up a widget's value, for drilling in. Writes nothing.
Anyone who may read the dashboard.

200.description: The exact records behind the widget's value or bucket, with an exact total

404.description: No such dashboard, nothing is published, or the widget is not in the executed definition

422.description: The widget is not exactly drillable, the key does not apply, or the count exceeds the cost ceiling

x-audit-exempt.note: Dashboard 10/10 Phase 3.1: lists the records behind a widget value over the caller's record scope and writes nothing.

post.description: A person picks which of the decision's options runs. Needs update rights on decisions. Audited.

409.description: Not proposed, or row_version is stale

422.description: chosen_option_id does not belong to this decision

post.description:
Runs the approved option through the platform's one action path, with its gate, and records the
invocation and its result on the decision. Audited.

403.description: Caller lacks the required privilege, or the option's action requires an approved approval request

404.description: No such decision, option, or action

409.description: Not approved, or row_version is stale

422.description: The option's stored arguments failed validation

post.summary: Read a page of an embedded dashboard
post.description:
P8-T1: public; the signed viewer token is the credential. Answers the
page's widgets as the embed's creator sees them, with the token's fixed
parameters, and only the embed's sites may frame it.

401.description: A token that is malformed, forged or expired

404.description: The embed was stopped, or no such page

x-audit-exempt.note: reads one embedded dashboard page; writes nothing

get.description:
Every active metric definition with the queries it reads, one-based pages. Anyone who may read
metric definitions.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description:
One-based (D-347): page 1 is the first page. Values below 1 are
clamped up to 1 rather than rejected, matching the legacy lists.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description:
Rows per page, clamped to `1..=MAX_PAGE_SIZE`. Defaults to
`DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE`.

post.summary: Build a metric from its parts
post.description:
P9-T3: describes the metric as an entity, an aggregate over one of its
attributes, the date that places a record in the metric's period, filters
and dimensions; creates (or republishes) the metric's stored query from it
and points the metric at that query. Needs the metric's update privilege.

200.description: The metric reads the built query

409.description: The metric changed while it was being built

422.description: An unknown or sensitive attribute, a non-numeric measure, a bad filter, or a period without a calendar

post.description:
Computes the metric now instead of waiting for its schedule. Needs update rights on metric
definitions. Audited.

409.description: A compute for this metric/period is already in flight

422.description: Missing actual for a manual metric, formula source, or bad query_ref

post.summary: Compute a metric and everything under it
post.description:
P9-T8: computes every query and formula metric the metric is built from
(its children and its formula's inputs, transitively), children before
parents, then the metric itself, for each one's current period. One
metric's failure is reported and the rest go on; a cycle is refused.

200.description: What each metric of the tree did

get.description: What the metric reads (entities, attributes and other metrics) and what uses it (dashboard widgets, metrics), from the lineage graph; the counts preview what a change reaches (P10-T1).

get.summary: Read what a metric is made of
get.description:
The metric's composition for a period: its child metrics with their weights and, for a formula
metric, the metrics the formula uses, each with its latest snapshot. A cycle or a deep hierarchy
gives a cut-short tree, never an error. Anyone who may read metric definitions.

parameters.name: period_start
parameters.description:
The period to read snapshots for; defaults to the root metric's current
period.

200.description: The metric's children and formula inputs, each with its snapshot for the period

get.description:
Every value recorded for the metric, newest period first, superseded ones included, so a
restatement's whole history shows. Anyone who may read metric definitions.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: One-based: page 1 is the first page.

parameters.name: dimension_attribute
parameters.description:
A dimension attribute (comma-separated for several): its members'
rows instead of the totals.

post.summary: Spread a target to a dimension's members
post.description:
P9-T7: writes the period's total target and one child target per member
of the dimension, by the caller's shares or by last year's actuals. The
children add up to the total. Needs `attome_metric.set_target`.

409.description: A spread for this metric and period is running

422.description: Not one of the metric's dimensions, shares that do not add up to 1, or no actuals a year earlier

post.description: A new scenario copied from this one, to change and compare. Audited.

get.description:
This scenario and the ones in `with`, against every metric any of them uses: each cell is that
scenario's latest evaluated value, or `not_evaluated`. Needs read rights on scenarios.

parameters.name: with
parameters.description: Comma-separated additional scenario ids to compare against `{id}`.

404.description: No such scenario (the anchor `{id}`, or one named in `with`)

post.description: Computes the scenario's metrics and stores the results. Needs update rights on scenarios. Audited.

200.description: Success — see each result's `status`/`note`. `ok` appears for a formula-backed metric that resolves against this scenario's assumptions (D-480/M27); `baseline_only`, `not_computable`, or `pending` cover every query/manual-backed metric per this module's own doc comment

404.description: No such scenario, or one it references a metric that no longer resolves

409.description: Another evaluate is already running for this scenario

oneOf.description: The action ran. `result` is the action's own payload.

Present only for actions that reach a model. `model_id` and
`prompt_version` ride here so the caller can log the outcome
against them (TODO-054) — provenance is not optional and cannot be
reconstructed later.

The gate requires a human to confirm this specific invocation before it
runs. **Nothing has executed and no side effect has occurred.**

proposal.description:
M35 v1 C3 — present only for an action that declares one
([`Action::confirmation_proposal`]): the normalized proposal, for
display only. Model-authored, so render it as untrusted plain
text. It carries no id, token or handle and authorizes nothing:
confirming means the human invoking the action themselves.

oneOf.description:
The gate requires four-eyes approval (D-195). Nothing has executed;
`dispatch` has already raised the `attome_approval` request itself (the
gate decision's own doc comment always said this — closing the gap
where nothing actually did it). `approval_id` is the handle a caller
polls or an approver UI lists.

AH8: held for its undo window. Nothing has executed yet; it runs at
`run_at` unless cancelled (`POST /api/v1/ai/deferred-actions/{id}/cancel`)
and is re-checked first.

V2-D702: staged for the person's review with the session's other
staged actions. Nothing has executed, and nothing will until they
apply it (`POST /api/v1/ai/deferred-actions/apply`).

approval_pending.description:
`true` when `dashboard.publish` is in
`approval.required_actions` and this call only submitted a pending
four-eyes request; the live version is unchanged until it is decided.

field.description:
`"query_id"` or `"view_id"` — which column this broken reference came
from.

reason.description:
`"invalid_format"` (not a UUID at all) or `"not_found"` (well-formed,
but no active row of the referenced kind has that id).

value.description: The raw stored value that failed to resolve.

oneOf.description: The single bucket of an ungrouped definition.
A group whose stored value is not NULL, as PostgreSQL renders it as text.
The group of rows whose field is NULL.

A time bucket: `start ≤ t < end`, both UTC instants computed in the
resolved timezone.

BucketKey.description:
A bucket's identity: the stored value, never a display string, so a drill
predicate can be rebuilt from it exactly (D-522 decision 11).

query_id.description: The stored query the metric now reads.

choice_styles.description:
Per-value color/icon presentation hints for a `data_type: "choice"`
column — the raw `choice_styles` map from `attome_field::ChoiceOptions`,
keyed by choice value. `None` for every other column, and for a
choice column with no configured styles. Metadata-derived, set
alongside `data_type` in the enrichment loop below.

lookup_target_entity.description:
Logical name of the entity a `data_type: "lookup"` column points to —
`None` for every other column. Metadata-derived (never from
`table_definition`), set alongside `data_type` in the enrichment loop
below. The frontend turns this into a route
(`logicalToUrlPath`) to make an unconfigured lookup cell clickable by
default — a plain logical name, not a route, so this crate stays free
of Angular's routing scheme.

CompareMetricColumn.description:
`pub` (this struct and the three below, fields too) — `do_compare`
returns this directly and this crate's own `tests/scenario.rs` inspects
it, same reasoning as `ScenarioResultRow` above.

cells.description:
Aligned by index with the response's `metrics` array — a `null`-shaped
entry (`status = "not_evaluated"`) stands in for a metric this
scenario references but has never run `evaluate` for.

actual.description:
Required when the metric is `source_kind = "manual"`; ignored for
`"query"`.

force.description:
When `true`, always writes a new snapshot — D-407's restatement path
— chained via `superseded_ref` to whatever was there before, which is
left untouched.

period_start.description:
Defaults to the metric's current period (today's day/week/month/
quarter/year boundary, UTC).

skipped.description:
`true` when an existing snapshot was returned unchanged (idempotent
skip) rather than a new one being computed.

ComputeTreeResponse.description: A tree computation, in the order it ran.

pages.description:
Same shape `pages_snapshot` produces — every `id` may be omitted, a
fresh one is always generated (`IdPolicy::GenerateNewIds`).

DataContract.description: D-525 — the data a widget type is built on.

DefinitionSource.description: Where the executed definition came from.

pages_needing_root_section.description:
Pages with no active section — reported, never repaired on read
(D-527); `POST .../pages/{page_id}/root-section` repairs one.

sections.description: Every active section under those pages, ordered by `sequence`, then id.

widgets.description: Every active widget under those sections, ordered by `sequence`, then id.

target_section_id.description:
Defaults to the source widget's own `section_id` when omitted —
"duplicate in place" and "paste into another section" are the same
call with/without this field.

record_id.description: Populated by whatever record page embeds this dashboard (Phase 14).

EmbedRead.description: A page of an embedded dashboard to read.

ErrorDetails.description:
`ErrorResponse.details`: its shape depends on the `error` code —
a list of [`FieldError`] on `validation_error`, [`RuleViolationDetails`] on
`rule_violation`, [`FieldLockedDetails`] on `field_locked` and
`field_locked_required` (D-789).

ErrorResponse.description: Standard error envelope. `error` is a stable machine-readable code; `message` is human-readable and never contains internal detail.

current_state.description:
Present on a version conflict: the server's current row for the
fields the caller touched, as a JSON object. The owning engine filters
sensitive columns out before building it (BTY-16c's precondition), so
this is a deliberate filtered projection — never a raw row dump.

current_version.description:
Present on a version conflict: the `row_version` the server currently
holds, so a caller can re-read and retry instead of guessing what the
winner wrote. Omitted when the conflict is not version-based.

oneOf.description:
Structured detail, shaped by `error` (see [`ErrorDetails`]): every
field-level failure on a `validation_error` response when the raiser
has a field list, so a form can render them all at once; every firing
rule on a `rule_violation` response from a business rule; every
refused field on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required`. Omitted
otherwise.

error.description:
Stable machine-readable code — `not_found`, `unauthorized`, `forbidden`,
`attribute_not_writable`, `limit_exceeded`,
`conflict`, `version_conflict`, `duplicate_detected`, `idempotency_conflict`,
`validation_error`, `customer_tests_failed`, `feature_unavailable`, `feature_hidden`,
`rate_limit_exceeded`, `overloaded`, `capability_unavailable`,
`metadata_authoring_locked`, `transition_not_allowed`,
`rule_violation`, `field_locked`, `field_locked_required`,
`reauth_required`, `server_timeout`, `query_timeout`, `read_only`, `payload_too_large`,
`request_rejected`, `invalid_cursor`, `resync_needed`, `cascade_restricted`,
`idempotency_outcome_unknown`, `idempotency_replay_unavailable`,
`method_not_allowed`, or
`internal_error` — one per `AppError` variant (`FieldLocked` answers
two: plain and required) (`attome-types/src/error.rs`); M01 Core C-23
found this list four codes short of the taxonomy it documents.

errors.description:
Every field-level failure on a `validation_error`, as
`{attribute, rule, message, fix}`.

field.description:
Present on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required` (D-789): the first
refused field (every one is in `details.fields`); on
`attribute_not_writable` (Q15-T4): the attribute the caller may not
write.

hidden.description:
Present on `duplicate_detected`: how many more matches the caller may
not read.

instance.description: The request path the problem happened at.

matches.description:
Present on `duplicate_detected` (A15-T4): the existing records the
save matches that the caller may read (record, rule, score).

request_id.description:
Present on responses that passed through the request-id middleware
(D-043); absent on the few pre-middleware rejection paths.

retry_after_sec.description:
Present on a `rate_limit_exceeded` response when the limiter knows its
window: seconds to wait before retrying, equal by construction to the
`Retry-After` header on the same response (BTY-11a). Omitted when the
limit that was hit has no known window.

retryable.description:
Whether the same request may succeed later (the error catalogue's
verdict for `code`).

rule_id.description:
Present on a `rule_violation` response (D-472): the id of the
`xrm_core_rule` whose failing expression produced this 422, so a
client can highlight or re-check the exact rule without parsing
`message`. Omitted on every other code, and on any response that
does not name a rule.
Also present on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required` (D-789): the
business rule that locks `field`.

rule_name.description:
Present on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required`: the display name
of the rule that locks `field`.

title.description:
A short title for `code` in the request's language (Z14-T3), e.g.
`The resource was not found.`

type.description: Z14-T1 (RFC 9457): `about:blank`; the problem is named by `code`.

next_cursor.description:
Present only in cursor mode: the `after_id` value the caller passes
back to fetch the next page. `None` means either OFFSET mode, or
cursor mode with no further rows (the page came back short).

total.description:
`None` in keyset/cursor mode (P1.11(g)) — `COUNT(*) OVER()` scans the
full matching set regardless of OFFSET vs keyset, a cost independent
of (and additional to) the O(offset) problem keyset fixes, so cursor
requests skip it rather than pay for a total the typical cursor
caller (export/infinite-scroll/API integration) doesn't need.

total_estimated.description:
A13-T2: `true` when `total` is the planner's estimate rather than a
count: a matching set of [`EXACT_TOTAL_LIMIT`] rows or more is not
counted, as counting it would scan it all.

can_edit_query.description:
The caller may open the admin query editor for this exact query.
Query mutations are currently system.admin-only, so derive this from
the same authoritative SecurityContext that authorized execution.

entity_logical_name.description:
Logical name resolved from the query's entity UUID link. Clients use
this to derive generic list/form routes without hardcoded entity URLs.

view_id.description: Presentation view used for this execution. Raw query executions have no view.

view_kind.description:
D-429's view `kind` (chart follow-up, migration 0447) — `None` when
this execution has no bound view. Lets a non-admin client (e.g. the
dashboard widget viewer) render `kind`-specific settings without a
second, admin-gated call — see `SqlQueryRow::view_kind`'s doc comment.

value_display.description:
A readable value where one is safe to show: a built-in `@current_user`
shows only the caller's own user name.

FieldError.description:
One field-level failure inside `ErrorResponse.details` (BTY-16b): the
field the caller sent, a stable machine-readable `code` the client maps
to localized text (e.g. `required`, `too_long`, `invalid_format`,
`not_allowed`), and the English server-side `message`.

A list, not a single error, so one 422 can answer with every bad field at
once (BTY-F11) instead of making a form discover them one round-trip at a
time.

code.description:
Stable machine-readable failure code for this field, independent of
the message text.

field.description:
The offending field, as the caller addressed it (e.g. `email` or
`amount`).

message.description: Human-readable, English, server-side detail for this field.

FieldLockedDetails.description:
`details` of a `field_locked` / `field_locked_required` response: every
refused field, the first being the one the top-level `field` names.

Filter.description:
P-api-contract Phase 0 disclosure: the retired hand-written
`openapi/query-v1.json` declared `op` as a JSON-schema `enum` of the 8
operator strings in this doc comment. Reproducing an exact `enum`
constraint on a plain `String` field (as opposed to a real Rust enum)
needs utoipa's `schema_with` escape hatch, whose exact builder-call shape
this session could not verify against the installed utoipa version — no
Rust toolchain in this sandbox (see the `no-rust-toolchain` memory /
DECISIONS.md entry for this change). Left as a documented, lower-fidelity
field (doc comment + example) rather than guessing at unverified macro
internals; re-add the `enum` constraint via `schema_with` once a human
can compile-check it — tracked as a Phase 0 follow-up, not silently
dropped. Runtime validation is unaffected either way: every caller's own
`match f.op.as_str()` is untouched by this OpenAPI-only annotation.

op.description:
One of: `contains`, `starts_with`, `ends_with`, `contains_any`,
`contains_all`, `eq`, `neq`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `in`,
`is_null`, `is_not_null`. `starts_with`/`ends_with` are text-only,
like `contains`; `neq` excludes a stored NULL (SQL `<>`), exactly like
every other comparison — `is_null` is the only way to match one. The
four were added by D-607 (advanced find, B-R10 Phase A): the entity
grid had offered them since C-28 while the server refused them. For a
multi-select Choice:
`contains` tests one option, `contains_any` matches any supplied
option, and `contains_all` matches every supplied option. `in` matches
any of a non-empty string array by typed equality (not valid for a
multi-select Choice). `is_null` takes no value and matches a stored
NULL — the only way to express a NULL bucket (dashboard 10/10 Phase 0
spike S1). `under` and `above` (A17-T2) take a record id for a lookup
into a tree (an entity with one parent lookup to itself) and match
that record and everything below it, or above it, up to 32 levels.
`tagged` (B4-T4) takes a tag id on the `id` field and matches the
records carrying that tag (a personal tag only for its owner).
`within_km` (A2-T3) takes `"lat,lng,km"` (or `{lat, lng, km}`) on a
geolocation field and matches the points at most `km` kilometres
away; a geolocation field takes no other operator but `is_null` and
`is_not_null`.

value.description:
Scalar filters retain the v1 string contract. Multi-select Choice
filters additionally accept a JSON string array for `contains_any`
and `contains_all`; `in` takes a string array; `is_null` ignores it.

FilterOrigin.description:
Where an applied filter came from — carried to the response so the
explanation (Phase 3.2) and the records drill use the same list.

oneOf.description: Present only for a time bucket; the field must then be a date field.

blocking.description:
Phase 3.5 — what refuses publish; empty from `do_health_check` alone,
filled by the health route.

checked.description:
Non-empty `query_id`/`view_id` references checked across this
dashboard's widgets — a widget declaring both counts as two; a widget
declaring neither (rich text, dividers, …) is not counted at all.

live_snapshot_format.description: D-543 — the live snapshot's format. `None` when nothing is live.

live_version_dependencies.description:
D-521 — the query versions the **live** version is pinned to, and
whether each has been superseded. Empty when nothing is live or the
live snapshot predates pinning (snapshot format 1).

partially_pinned.description:
True when something is live but its snapshot predates format 3, so some
of what viewers see is still resolved live (view semantics, column
metadata, parameters, variables), or predates format 4 while it has
governed KPI widgets (D-544). Cleared by republishing.

publishable.description: Whether publish would pass the gate now.

warnings.description: Phase 3.5 — what is reported but never blocks.

service_scoped.description:
Always true: governed KPIs are computed by the platform service account
for a fixed scope, never filtered to the viewer (D-522 decision 5).

Always true: computed by the platform service account for a fixed scope,
never filtered to the viewer, and never drillable to records.

history.description: Newest first; a trendline's series, empty for a scorecard.

pinned_query_version_id.description: The query version a published query-backed metric is held to.

LockedField.description:
One field a business rule locks for the writer (D-789 §3.5): `effect` is
`hidden` or `disabled`. No value is ever echoed.

MetricConsumer.description: One thing that uses a metric.

MetricImpact.description: What a metric is made of and what a change to it reaches.

downstream.description: Everything that references the metric, by kind (at most 500).

impact.description: How many consumers of each kind a change reaches.

attribute.description: The attribute, when the input is one attribute of the entity.

entity.description: The entity's logical name (an entity input).

children.description:
`no_recursion`: the node is recursive, and without it building the
OpenAPI document expands it inline forever (same fix as
`attome_dashboard::layout::SnapshotSection`).

cycle.description: This metric already appears higher up the tree; it is not expanded again.

metric_id.description: `None` for a formula reference to a key no active metric carries.

missing.description: A formula reference that names no active metric.

oneOf.description: The latest snapshot for the lineage period; `null` when none exists.

truncated.description: The depth limit stopped the walk here.

weight.description: A child's weight in its parent.

MetricParity.description: P7-T2: a drilled KPI's snapshot next to the records listed now.

as_of_available.description:
Whether the records as they were when the snapshot was taken can be
listed; never yet.

counts_records.description:
Whether the metric counts records, so the snapshot and the listed
total are the same measure and can be compared.

listed_total.description: How many records the caller may read match the definition now.

period_start.description: The period the records were listed for: the metric's current one.

snapshot_value.description: The latest snapshot of that period; absent before one is computed.

MetricSpec.description: A metric described by its parts.

date_attribute.description:
The date that places a record in a period: a date or date-time
attribute, or `created_at` / `modified_at`.

dimension_attributes.description: Attributes the value is broken down by, at most three.

measure_attribute.description: The attribute aggregated; optional for `count` (every record).

NewDashboardFields.description:
The scalar `attome_dashboard` fields a `create_from_layout` caller supplies
— deliberately narrower than the full column set `lifecycle.rs`'s
`DashboardFieldsRow` snapshots (no `organization_id`/`thumbnail`/
`settings`/`is_template`/`template_category`/`template_version`): those
are either operator-scoped concerns an authoring caller has no basis to
set, or edited afterward through ordinary generic entity CRUD once the
dashboard exists.

allowed_origins.description: `https://` origins that may frame the dashboard.

NewPageBody.description:
The page fields a caller may set when adding a page. `dashboard_id` is not
accepted — it always comes from the path — and neither are sections, which
the page gets exactly one of (D-527).

parameters.description: The dashboard parameters this viewer is fixed to.

ttl_secs.description: Seconds the token lives: 1 to 3600, 600 by default.

widgets.description: One entry per widget on the page, in layout order.

PaginatedResponse_MetricDefinitionSummar.description: The platform's canonical list envelope (guidelines §12). `total` is the size of the whole set, not of `items`. `page` echoes the page served; every offset list is one-based (D-793): page 1 is the first page. `warnings` is sent only when there is one (Z14-T6).

lineage_entities.description:
Entities this metric's query touches, when `source_kind = "query"` —
empty for manual/formula metrics or a query with no declared mapping.

warnings.description:
Z14-T6: what the caller should know though the list succeeded;
omitted when empty.

PaginatedResponse_SnapshotRow.description: The platform's canonical list envelope (guidelines §12). `total` is the size of the whole set, not of `items`. `page` echoes the page served; every offset list is one-based (D-793): page 1 is the first page. `warnings` is sent only when there is one (Z14-T6).

definition_fingerprint.description:
P9-T9: [`definition_fingerprint`] of the definition fields at compute
time; `None` on rows written before P9-T9.

definition_version.description: P9-T9: the definition version the value was computed under.

dimension_attribute.description:
P9-T5: `None` on the total row; on a member row, the dimension
attribute(s), comma-separated.

dimension_value.description: The member's value (several dimensions' values comma-separated).

warnings.description:
Z14-T6: what the caller should know though the list succeeded;
omitted when empty.

Parity.description: P7-T4: a drill's listed total beside the widget's number.

value.description:
The widget's number for the drilled bucket; absent when there is none
to compare.

ParityReason.description:
P7-T4: why a drill's listed total and the widget's number differ, or
that they agree.

PinnedDependencyStatus.description:
D-521 — one widget's pinned query version in the live snapshot. A pinned
dashboard keeps running `pinned_version_id` until it is republished;
`newer_version_available` tells an editor that a republish would pick up a
changed query. `query_active` false means the pinned SQL will not run at
all (pinned SQL, live security).

Presentation.description: Modifiers applied on the server over the computed buckets.

other_bucket.description:
Fold the groups past `limit` into one explicit Other bucket. Needs
`limit` and a plain field group.

oneOf.description:
Defaults to `value_desc` for a field group and `key_asc` for a time
bucket. Ties always break on the typed key, then the series key.

suggestion_id.description:
The row in `ai_suggestion_outcome` this suggestion was logged as.
The caller reports the human's decision against it.

approval_pending.description:
`true` when `dashboard.publish` is in `approval.required_actions` and
this call only submitted a pending four-eyes request — the fields
below are `None` in that case, and the dashboard is still `approved`,
not `published`, until a second admin decides the request.

PublishedDashboard.description: D-521 — what a viewer of `dashboard_id` sees.

snapshot.description:
The version snapshot (`snapshot_format` 2 carries pinned
`dependencies`); `null` for `none`.

rows_are_the_result.description:
True when the rows shown are the result (a query over more than one
entity); false when its buckets drill to records (P7-T1).

RenderKind.description:
D-525 — how the viewer renders a widget type. Only types with a real
renderer carry anything but `unsupported`; the palette hides the rest and an
existing widget of such a type renders an explicit "unsupported widget type"
state (and is reported by health).

page_id.description:
Scopes which declared `dashboard_variable`/`dashboard_parameter`
rows apply — omit for dashboard-level only.

RuleFailure.description:
One business-rule `error` policy that fired (D-789 §3.3), inside a
`rule_violation` body's `details.rules`. Carries names and the rule's own
message, never a record value.

field.description: The field the policy is attached to, when it names one.

rule_name.description: The rule's display name (its name when it has none).

RuleViolationDetails.description:
`details` of a `rule_violation` response (D-789): the field of the first
failing policy, when it names one, and every blocking `error` policy that
fired, the first (by rule display order) being the one `rule_id` names.

ScenarioResultRow.description:
`pub` (fields too) — same reason `attome_metric::metric::SnapshotRow` is: `do_evaluate`
below returns these directly, and this crate's own `tests/scenario.rs`
reads their fields straight off the result of a direct call, the same
"call the `pub` `do_*` function, skip the HTTP layer" convention every
other suite in this crate already uses.

definition_fingerprint.description:
P9-T9: [`definition_fingerprint`] of the definition fields at compute
time; `None` on rows written before P9-T9.

definition_version.description: P9-T9: the definition version the value was computed under.

dimension_attribute.description:
P9-T5: `None` on the total row; on a member row, the dimension
attribute(s), comma-separated.

dimension_value.description: The member's value (several dimensions' values comma-separated).

children.description:
A section tree nests, so this type is recursive, and utoipa needs
`no_recursion` to stop expanding it inline — without it, building the
workspace OpenAPI document recurses until the stack overflows.
`attome_api::sidebar::SidebarItem::child` carries the identical
annotation for the identical reason; this one was missed, and the
symptom was `server --print-openapi` aborting with 0xC00000FD despite
`main.rs` already spawning a 64 MB stack for exactly this work.

The emitted schema still carries the `$ref` back to `SnapshotSection`,
so a generated client keeps the recursive type.

SnapshotWidget.description:
`pub` (struct and fields) — besides this module's own snapshot
round-trip, `create_from_layout`'s request body and this crate's own
tests construct these directly (see this module's doc comment's
"Write path" section and `do_create_from_layout`, below).

emits.description:
R-07 step 6 — same `#[serde(default)]` reasoning R-02 gave for
`view_id`: a snapshot written before this field existed must still
deserialize. Omitted here, publish/restore/clone silently dropped a
widget's event wiring.

value.description: A scalar; a list for `in`; none for `is_null` and `is_not_null`.

dimension_attribute.description: One of the metric's dimension attributes.

period_start.description: The period the targets are for (its start).

shares.description: With `share`: each member's share, summing to 1.

label.description:
A display label derived from the key: the value itself, a lookup
value's target record name when the caller may read it, or the bucket
start in the resolved timezone. `null` for NULL, Total and Other — the
client localizes those.

oneOf.description: `Value`/`Null` only; present when the definition has a series.

series_label.description: The series value's display label, on the same rules as `label`.

values.description:
One value per measure, in definition order. `null` when the measure has
no value for the group (an average over no numeric values).

raw_values.description:
The values before cumulative / percent / moving-average rewrote them,
one row per bucket; absent when nothing was rewritten.

truncated.description: Groups past the limit exist; with `other` they are folded, not dropped.

access_level.description:
The caller's read depth on the entity: `global`, `business_unit`,
`team` or `none` (own and shared records only).

live_rows_only.description: Inactive records never count (`is_active` NULL or true).

StructuredRecords.description:
A drill-through result set: column metadata, rows, the read instant and the
filters that reproduce it, keyset-paged by `next_cursor`. Like
`query/execute`'s tabular shape it is a documented exception to
`CursorPage<T>` (guidelines §12): the metadata around the rows is part of
the contract, so it is not a plain item list.

drill_filters.description:
The definition, binding and bucket predicates as concrete filters, so an
export reproduces exactly these rows. Absent for the Other bucket, whose
NULL-aware complement no filter list can express.

next_cursor.description: Pass back as `after_id` for the next page; absent on the last page.

rows.description: One JSON object per record, keyed by column name.

total.description:
Exact: a count over the same scope and drill predicate as the rows,
never an estimate.

TreeComputed.description: One metric of a tree computation.

outcome.description: `computed`, `skipped` (a snapshot for the period existed) or `failed`.

TreeRecord.description:
One row of the draft tree, in the same `{id, row_version, data}` shape the
generic entity list returns, so the editor can keep sending `If-Match`
updates through generic CRUD with the `row_version` it read here.

config.description: The raw `dashboard_widget.config` payload a client is about to save.

widget_type.description:
The widget type the config is for. Omitted means `declarative_widget`,
this route's original contract. For any other type the route checks
that the type is renderable and validates `config.data` (a structured
definition) and `config.bindings` (dashboard 10/10 Phase 2.1).

Warning.description:
Something the server did that the caller should know about though the
request succeeded (a value truncated, a default applied, a page clamped):
a stable `code` and English `message`. Sent only when there is one.

applied_filters.description: Every filter the number was computed with, and where each came from.

definition_fingerprint.description: Stable for identical definitions and inputs.

deprecated_alias_of.description:
D-479 (M26 R-09) — set when `type_id` is a legacy id kept only so an
already-migrated `dashboard_widget.widget_type` value (written by
the now-deleted legacy dashboard-migration job, D-790) still resolves
to a real descriptor.
Names the modern `type_id` a viewer should actually render this
widget with — the palette/builder should offer the modern id, not
this one, for a brand-new widget. `None` for every non-legacy
descriptor.

render_kind.description:
D-525 — filled in by [`WidgetRegistry::register`] from the renderer
table (an alias inherits its target's), so no descriptor can claim a
renderer the viewer does not have.

schema.description:
Descriptive only — see this module's doc comment for why no schema
enforcement exists yet.

type_id.description:
Matches one value in `dashboard_widget.widget_type`'s choice list
(`seed.rs`) — the two must stay in sync, which is why `seed.rs` reads
its choice list from [`WidgetRegistry::type_ids`] rather than
duplicating this table.

WidgetInputs.description: What a viewer may send to a data route: values, never definitions.

cross_filters.description:
Cross-filter variable values by name. Only variables the widget listens
to apply; the rest are ignored, so one page-wide map serves every widget.

page_size.description: Row page size for a query-backed (Class C) widget, 1–200.

parameters.description:
Values for declared dashboard parameters, by name. A `date_range`
parameter takes `{ "start": "YYYY-MM-DD", "end": "YYYY-MM-DD" }`; every
other type takes a string (a number may also be a JSON number). `null`
or an omitted name falls back to the declared default.

preview.description:
Execute the editor's draft instead of the published version. Needs
record Update on the dashboard; without it the dashboard reads as
missing (404).

WidgetRecordsInputs.description:
What a viewer may send to the records route: the data route's values plus
which bucket to list.

after_id.description: Keyset cursor: the `next_cursor` of the previous page.

oneOf.description:
A bucket key exactly as the data route returned it; omitted lists every
row the (ungrouped) number covers.

applied_filters.description: The same filters the number was computed with, and their origins.

definition_fingerprint.description: Equal to the data route's fingerprint for the same inputs.

oneOf.description: P7-T2: for a KPI widget, the snapshot and the records listed now.

parity.description:
P7-T4: whether the listed total equals the widget's number, and why
not.

some_records_hidden.description:
P7-T3: for a KPI widget, whether the caller's read scope on the
metric's entity is narrower than the whole entity the metric was
computed over, so the number counts records this list leaves out.
Only the flag: how many are hidden is never counted or returned.

portal_session.name: __Secure-wp_{portal}_session
portal_session.description: A web portal user's session cookie, issued by the portal's sign-in; `{portal}` is the portal's keyword (`wp_{portal}_session` on plain-http local dev). Valid only on that portal's own routes.

s2s_hmac.name: x-s2s-signature
s2s_hmac.description: A system-to-system call, signed. Send `x-s2s-client-id`, `x-s2s-key-id`, `x-s2s-timestamp` (Unix milliseconds, within 300 seconds of the server's clock), `x-s2s-nonce` (single use: a repeat is refused) and `x-s2s-signature`: the hex HMAC-SHA256, keyed by the hex-decoded client secret, of `METHOD`, `PATH_AND_QUERY`, the hex SHA-256 of the body, `TIMESTAMP` and `NONCE`, joined by newlines in that order.

session_cookie.name: __Host-session_token
session_cookie.description: Browser session cookie issued by POST /api/v1/auth/login. Mutating requests additionally require the CSRF conditions enforced by `middleware::csrf`.
